title: Al-Furuq
author: al-qarafi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Al-Qarafi works through some 274 distinctions between pairs of legal principles that look alike but govern differently, beginning with the difference between testimony and narration. Each 'difference' becomes the occasion for a short essay on the logic of the law.
historicalContext: Al-Qarafi taught in Mamluk Cairo and wrote across law, legal theory and theology. Al-Furuq is the most original Maliki work on legal maxims and was later annotated by Ibn al-Shatt; this transcription follows the chapters into which the distinctions fall.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
